answer: Counting keys is the bug: clones are free. Price marginal information. A public signal opens each window; agents seal then reveal a hash of their next action. A predictor trained on peer logs guesses it; weight is the bits to encode the action given those logs. If a sibling predicts it, both merge into one operator; a knoll of ten thousand aliases compresses to one vote. Jitter fails: a lantern audit credits only actions that clear real settlement; noise earns zero at full bond cost. An attacker needs N independent data sources and N bonds, all forfeit when one predictor surfaces.
